proof:
Let $P$ be the old positive integer bases. By 55a57b1cf55d0c87 applied to the compatible old nonempty sections, $P=\operatorname{conv}P\cap\mathbb Z^n$. A common bounded region contains all $C_t$ for sufficiently small $t$, hence their nonempty sections occur in a common finite integer envelope $R$. For $r\in R\setminus P$ every cluster point of a sequence in $(C_t)_r$ belongs to $C_r$ by ambient convergence. Thus, if $C_r$ is nonempty, the section is eventually contained in any fixed neighborhood of the compact null set $C_r$, whose shrinking neighborhoods have volumes tending to zero. If $C_r$ is empty, compactness of the common bounded region forces eventual emptiness. Hence the total mass on $R\setminus P$ tends to zero. Each such integer $r$ is outside $\operatorname{conv}P$. A fixed closed pure-base halfspace separating it strictly from that hull covers its whole plane and has new mass bounded by the total mass on $R\setminus P$.

The section convergence on $P$ implies convergence in volume of the symmetric differences, since a Hausdorff-close pair of positive convex bodies retains a common smaller old interior ball and each body lies inside a homothetic enlargement of the other about that ball's center, with ratios tending to one. Together with the exterior mass estimate this implies $M_t\to M>0$ and uniform convergence of cap masses over all fixed-normal thresholds, since their differences are bounded by the summed symmetric-difference volumes and the new exterior mass. For any selected cap through an own-interior old anchor, its old centered interior ball retains a smaller concentric ball for all nearby families. Near the old threshold, its nonzero continuous normal cuts that ball in interior sections. The cap mass is continuous in threshold because every section plane is $d$-volume null. Increasing the threshold across any nontrivial subinterval of this neighborhood removes a positive slab of that ball, so the mass is strictly decreasing there. Taking thresholds on both sides of the old one gives a common neighborhood of old masses in which the local inverse $b_{ij}(t,\tau)$ exists and decreases continuously and strictly. The same strict bracketing and uniform convergence of masses show convergence of these inverses to their old values at each nearby fixed mass.

For any one circuit the weighted inverse sum is also strictly decreasing and continuous. At the old mass it equals the old weighted threshold. Bracket this value on either side of the old mass using the old inverse, and retain the brackets for small $t$ by convergence. This proves existence, uniqueness and convergence of the common mass root. The resulting weighted margin is still $A_i\cdot z-h_i$. If it is nonnegative, at least one adjusted closed cap contains $(z,x)$ for every $x$.

At each $p\in P\setminus I$ use 755cb08c379113cc at an old fiber maximum, with old common mass $q_p\in(0,Q)$ and an interior anchor by 55a57b1cf55d0c87. The same inverse construction gives a new group covering the whole plane there and still strictly slack compared with $\max_i\tau_i(t)$, since its common mass tends to $q_p$. The fixed-face lemma covers every old deepest plane using the selected groups, and the pure-base separators cover every other site in $R$ at vanishing mass. Finiteness and $\max_i\tau_i(t)\to Q>0$ make the latter caps slack as well. Each actual new point lies in a cap of mass at most $\max_i\tau_i(t)$. Division by $M_t$ proves the comparison, and the old maximum gives equality at zero.
statement: Use the ordinary mixed setting, fixed deepest witnesses and arbitrary chosen circuits of the fixed-face critical-circuit lemma. Suppose compact convex $C_t\to C$ in ambient Hausdorff distance and, at each old positive integer base $p$, $(C_t)_p\to C_p$ in Hausdorff distance. Let $M_t$ be the total summed $d$-volume of the actual integer fibers of $C_t$. Retain each selected cap normal and each circuit weight. For the $i$th deepest group there is a unique nearby common raw mass $\tau_i(t)\to Q$ whose local inverse mass thresholds $b_{ij}(t,\tau_i(t))$ satisfy $\sum_j\rho_{ij} b_{ij}(t,\tau_i(t))=h_i$, the original weighted threshold. The adjusted caps still cover the whole plane over every $z$ in the original projected group halfspace $A_i\cdot z\ge h_i$. For all sufficiently small $t$ the maximum normalized ordinary depth of the actual mixed set of $C_t$ is at most $\max_i\tau_i(t)/M_t$, with equality at $t=0$.
title: Exact ordinary quantile covers with emerging integer fibers
